proposals.before: A granddaughter of Yuwen Jiong was exceptionally beautiful and was already in the palace.
proposals.after: A granddaughter of Yuchi Jiong was exceptionally beautiful and was already in the palace.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉遲迥 is Yuchi Jiong, not the Yuwen clan; the idiomatic English misidentifies the surname.

proposals.after: A granddaughter of Yuchi Jiong had beautiful looks and was already in the palace.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉遲迥 is Yuchi Jiong; the literal English repeats the same surname error.

proposals.after: Gao Jiong, Yang Su, and others overtook him, seized his horse's bridle, and remonstrated with him in desperate earnest.

decisions.reason: s0127 has 尉遲迥女孫; 尉遲 is the Xianbei surname Yuchi, not Yuwen (宇文). The proposed Yuchi Jiong correctly identifies the grandfather named in the kinship phrase.
The literal likewise misreads 尉遲迥 as Yuwen Jiong; Yuchi Jiong is the correct romanization of the same Chinese name.
s0131 names 高熲; 熲 is read Jiǒng, so Gao Jiong is required. Feng is a mistransliteration of that character.
s0133 attributes the speech to 高熲; the speaker must be Gao Jiong, not Gao Feng.
s0138 again names 高熲 as the father's household guest; Gao Jiong restores the correct personal name.
s0143 has 黜高熲; the official dismissed is Gao Jiong. Feng remains a mistransliteration of 熲.
s0136 shortens the name to 熲 beside 素; the given-name reference must be Jiong, matching Gao Jiong, not Feng.
s0139 has 聞熲謂己為一婦人; the short reference 熲 is Jiong, not Feng.
s0140 has 熲夫人; the possessive short form of 高熲 must be Jiong's, not Feng's.
s0164 names 兵部尚書柳述; 述 is Shù, so Liu Shu is correct and Xu misreads the given name.
The idiomatic ends with a stray closing quotation mark after “auspicious” with no matching opener for that clause; removing it restores clean punctuation without changing meaning.

claimRetractions.reason: English Yuwen Jiong exists only from the bad idiomatic/literal misreading of 尉遲迥; accepting r0001 restores Yuchi Jiong (already claimed in c0097) and leaves no source support for a Yuwen personal name.
English Gao Feng exists only from mistransliterating 熲; accepting r0003 restores Gao Jiong (already claimed in c0105) and leaves no source support for Feng as this person's name.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0009 shows English Feng's principal wife came only from the bad short form of 熲夫人; the title claim must read Jiong's principal wife while keeping id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0010 shows English Liu Xu came only from misreading 述; the personal-name claim must read Liu Shu while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
